Gravesham's population increased by around 5,200 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 110,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Gravesham increased by 5.1%, from around 101,700 in 2011 to around 106,900 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the South East (7.5%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Gravesham was home to around 7.7 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 7.3 in 2011. This area was among the top 45% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Gravesham than across the South East

Median age stable in Gravesham

The latest census data also show that the average (median) age remained 39 years in Gravesham between the last two censuses.

This area had a lower average (median) age than the South East as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a slightly lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just under 2,500 (an increase of 13.8%), while the number of residents between 20 and 24 years fell by around 850 (12.9% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.4 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Disability in Gravesham

The age-standardised proportion of residents who were identified as disabled and limited a little fell in Gravesham, but rose across the South East.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In Gravesham, the proportion of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a little fell from 10.3% in 2011 to 9.8% in 2021. During the same period, the regional proportion increased from 9.4% to 9.9%.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Gravesham fell from 8.6% to 7.3%, while the percentage of non-disabled residents increased from 81.1% to 82.9%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a little in Gravesham decreased by 0.5 percentage points

Gravesham residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 85,100 Gravesham residents said they were born in England. This represented 79.6% of the local population. The figure has decreased from around 85,800 in 2011, which at the time represented 84.4% of Gravesham's population.

India was the next most represented, with around 4,400 Gravesham residents reporting this country of birth (4.1%). This figure was up from around 4,000 in 2011, which at the time represented 3.9% of the population of Gravesham.

The number of Gravesham residents born in Nigeria rose from around 700 in 2011 (0.7% of the local population) to around 1,900 in 2021 (1.8%).

In 2021, 79.6% of Gravesham residents reported their country of birth as England

Ethnic groups in Gravesham

In 2021, 6.5% of Gravesham residents identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category, up from 2.8% in 2011. The 3.7 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South East, the percentage of people from the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" ethnic group increased from 1.6% to 2.4%, while across England the percentage increased from 3.5% to 4.2%.

In 2021, 76.6% of people in Gravesham identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 82.8% in 2011), while 11.2% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 10.4% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 1.9% in 2011 to 3.0% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 6.5% of usual residents in Gravesham identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category

National identity in Gravesham

In 2021, 11.3% of Gravesham residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 8.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.7%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.8% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Gravesham that identified as "British only" increased from 18.1% to 55.4%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater in Gravesham (2.4 percentage points) than across the South East (1.6 percentage points, from 7.1% to 8.7%). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Gravesham increased by 2.4 percentage points

Unpaid care in Gravesham

In 2021, 4.3% of Gravesham residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.0% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.9%) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.5% in 2011. The proportion of Gravesham residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 2.8% to 3.1%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Gravesham (2.7 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (2.8 percentage points, from 7.3% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Gravesham decreased by 2.7 percentage points

Religion in Gravesham

In 2021, 32.1% of Gravesham residents reported having "No religion", up from 21.5% in 2011. The rise of 10.6 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Gravesham. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South East, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.7% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 49.2% of people in Gravesham described themselves as Christian (down from 60.8%), while 8.0% described themselves as Sikh (up from 7.6% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 32.1% of usual residents in Gravesham reported having "No religion"

Fewer couples without children

In 2021, 14.1% of Gravesham households included a couple but no children. This figure decreased from 16.0% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in five households (21.4%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 21.5% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children increased from 7.2% to 7.9%.

This area had the region’s second lowest percentage of households including a couple but no children. Across the region, only Slough, with 10.5%, had a lower percentage.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Gravesham decreased by 1.9 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Gravesham residents aged 16 years and over, 35.8% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 32.4% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (46.8%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 48.9% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Gravesham that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership decreased from 8.7% to 8.6%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater in Gravesham (3.5 percentage points) than across the South East (2.9 percentage points, from 31.9% to 34.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Gravesham increased by 3.5 percentage points

Change in employment

Of Gravesham residents aged 16 years and over, 57.5% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, up from 57.3% in 2011.

While the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed increased here, across the South East the percentage fell from 59.0% in 2011 to 57.6% in 2021. Across England, the percentage fell from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Gravesham increased by 0.3 percentage points

Fewer adults working long hours

In 2021, 12.4% of Gravesham residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked over 49 hours per week. This figure decreased from 14.0% in 2011.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week was greater across the South East (2.7 percentage points, from 14.6% to 11.9%) than in Gravesham (1.6 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.2 percentage points, from 13.3% to 11.1%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults in employment who worked 49 hours or more in Gravesham decreased by 1.6 percentage points

Fall in home ownership

Of Gravesham households, 62.2% owned their home in 2021, down from 64.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in five households (19.1%) rented privately, compared with 16.1% in 2011. The percentage of Gravesham households that lived in a socially rented property increased from 17.3% to 17.4%.

The decrease in the percentage of households that owned their home in Gravesham (2.3 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (2.0 percentage points, from 67.6% to 65.7%). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.0 percentage points, from 63.3% to 61.3%.

The rate of home ownership in Gravesham decreased by 2.3 percentage points

Health in Gravesham

In 2021, 46.7% of Gravesham residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 43.7% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 35.8% to 34.9%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Gravesham residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.1% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 4.5% to 4.1%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Gravesham increased by 3.0 percentage points
